changeSet.author: nexus-rdr191.1
changeSet.comment:
nexus.gc_quarantine_orphans(dim, tenant, collection, quarantine_collection, quarantined_at, sample_limit) RETURNS TABLE(moved bigint, sample jsonb).
Moves every chunk in (tenant, collection) whose chash has no corresponding row in catalog_document_chunks for that (tenant, collection) into the quarantine sibling collection — an anti-join keyed on the chash PK column on both sides, no metadata read. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (destination) then DELETE (source): same copy-then-delete, upsert-on-collision contract as the Python quarantine_orphans() it replaces.
`sample` is capped at sample_limit entries: [{"chash": hex, "title": text-or-null}, ...] — for logging only, mirrors the Python orphan_sample cap (20). `moved` is the FULL count, uncapped, computed once from the same materialized DELETE RETURNING set the sample is drawn from (no second scan, no TOCTOU between count and sample).
SECURITY INVOKER under FORCE RLS — same admin/cross-tenant- capable shape as manifest_orphans (catalog-004): the caller (CatalogRepository, an authenticated per-tenant request context) passes tenant_id explicitly; RLS still governs actual row visibility/write eligibility via the nexus.tenant GUC set by the connection's tenant scope.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus.gc_quarantine_orphans(int, text, text, text, text, int)

changeSet.author: nexus-rdr191.1
changeSet.comment:
nexus.gc_restore_rereferenced(dim, tenant, quarantine_collection, origin_collection) RETURNS bigint — moves quarantined chunks whose chash IS referenced again by the manifest (a heal re-referenced them, or content returned) back to the origin collection. Mirrors Python restore_rereferenced()'s "mine" filter: a quarantine row with no `origin_collection` metadata stamp is treated as belonging to p_origin_collection (matches the Python `.get("origin_collection", collection_name)` default-to-self behaviour) via COALESCE(...) = p_origin_collection. Strips `quarantined_at`/`origin_collection` from the restored row's metadata (Python's `cleaned` pop of both keys). Same INSERT-then-DELETE, ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE collision handling as gc_quarantine_orphans, reversed direction.
Called BEFORE gc_quarantine_orphans in the GC pass — a fully- quarantined collection (origin emptied) must still be able to restore when a heal re-references its chashes (nexus-xukbj).
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus.gc_restore_rereferenced(int, text, text, text)

changeSet.author: nexus-rdr191.1
changeSet.comment: nexus.gc_expire_quarantine(dim, tenant, quarantine_collection, origin_collection, cutoff, floor_fraction, floor_min_chunks, force) RETURNS TABLE(expired bigint, refused bigint) — hard- deletes quarantine rows "belonging to" origin_collection (same COALESCE-to-self default as gc_restore_rereferenced) whose stamped `quarantined_at` is <= cutoff (a caller-formatted text timestamp, lexicographically comparable by construction — see file header). Carries the nexus-mr89x safety floor verbatim: a mass hard-delete surviving the FULL grace window is refused (expired=0, refused=N) unless floor_min_chunks/floor_fraction are not both exceeded, or force is true. Floor evaluation and the delete run in the SAME statement — no window between counting "mine"/"expired" and acting on them.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus.gc_expire_quarantine(int, text, text, text, text, float8, int, boolean)
